cluster: kind dataplane (1 control plane + 3 workers, v1.37.0)
service: svc-od (2) + svc-spot (2) behind Service checkout, PDB minAvailable=3

methodology.invalid_attempt: kubectl port-forward pins one TCP stream to one pod; a drain of a different pod cannot affect it, so that run was discarded.
methodology.valid_method: load generator runs as an in-cluster Job hitting http://checkout/work, so kube-proxy load-balances and endpoint updates are exercised.

measurements.case: graceful drain of the node hosting a spot pod
abrupt pod deletion (SIGKILL), 200 rps target, 200 ms requests
measurements.note: The harness did not observe loss at this scale: achieved 97.6 rps with ~20 requests in flight across 4 pods, so the killed pod held only a handful of connections and endpoint removal is fast. Reported as a limitation, not as evidence that abrupt loss is free.

conclusion: G4's zero-lost-request claim is supported for a planned drain with a 30 s notice, PDB and preStop hook. The abrupt case needs either a much higher request rate or per-pod connection pinning to measure; that is a follow-up, not a passed test.
